proposals.before: The doctors under the Grand Secretariat of Rites determined that the four deputy music supervisors, two music masters, two torchbearers, and two score keepers should all wear purple gauze official robes, black gauze futou with spread corners, red leather horn belts, wooden tablets, and black boots.
proposals.after: The doctors under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices determined that the four deputy music supervisors, two music masters, two torchbearers, and two score keepers should all wear purple gauze official robes, black gauze futou with spread corners, red leather horn belts, wooden tablets, and black boots.
proposals.reason: 太常寺 is the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, not the Grand Secretariat (中書/內閣).

proposals.after: Next came sixteen musicians in Five Blessings crowns and brocade robes, with six dragon flutes, six bili, and four zhanggu, joining the preceding Great Music in 《Gold-Letter Western Barbarian Sutra》.

decisions.reason: s0027 opens with 太常寺下博士議定; 太常寺 is the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, not the Grand Secretariat. The proposed idiomatic correctly renames the office while leaving the costume list intact.
The literal likewise misrenders 太常寺 as Grand Secretariat of Rites. Court of Imperial Sacrifices is the accurate institutional reading for this unit.
s0031 has 金太常寺掌故張珍; 太常寺 is the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under Jin, not a Grand Secretariat. The proposed idiomatic correctly restores Zhang Zhen's office title.
The literal repeats the same misreading of 金太常寺 as Grand Secretariat of Rites. Court of Imperial Sacrifices matches the Chinese office name.

s0037 has 中書吏部再準太常博士議定; 太常博士 are doctors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The proposed idiomatic correctly attributes the decision while preserving 中書吏部 as the Secretariat's Ministry of Personnel.
The literal likewise assigns 太常博士 to a Grand Secretariat of Rites. Court of Imperial Sacrifices is the correct institutional affiliation of those doctors.
s0278 lists 觱栗六 among the instruments; 觱栗/觱篥 is the bili double-reed pipe, not the suona (嗩吶). The proposed idiomatic correctly names the instrument.
The literal likewise mistranslates 觱栗 as suona. Bili is the accurate instrument name for this count of six.
